title: Month-End Rollover Allowances by Dining Plan
content:
Rollover percentage, rollover cap and money refund of unused credits, by plan of the Dining Plan:

| Plan | Share of unused credits at month end carried into the next month | Most credits carried into the next month | Unused credits refunded in money |
|---|---|---|---|
| Dining 10 Meal Plan | 0 percent | 0 | No |
| Dining 15 Meal Plan | 0 percent | 0 | No |
| Dining 30 Meal Plan | 25 percent | 5 | No |
| Dining 45 Meal Plan | 25 percent | 8 | No |
| Dining 60 Meal Plan | 50 percent | 10 | No |
| Dining Full Board Plan | 50 percent | 15 | No |

## Terms used in the table

- **Share carried into the next month** is a percentage of the credits left unused at the end of the month, and the credits it yields are rounded down to whole credits.
- **Most credits carried** is the ceiling on the credits carried into the next month, whatever the percentage yields.
- **Refunded in money**: on no plan of the Dining Plan are unused credits paid back in money.

## Points of reading

- On the Dining 10 Meal Plan and the Dining 15 Meal Plan the share is 0 percent and the ceiling 0, so no credits are carried into the next month on either plan.
- The fewest unused credits at month end at which the share alone reaches the ceiling are: 20 on the Dining 30 Meal Plan (25 percent of 20 is 5), 32 on the Dining 45 Meal Plan (25 percent of 32 is 8), 20 on the Dining 60 Meal Plan (50 percent of 20 is 10) and 30 on the Dining Full Board Plan (50 percent of 30 is 15). With more unused credits than that, the ceiling is the number carried.
- *Hypothetical:* 7 unused credits at month end on the Dining 45 Meal Plan give 25 percent of 7, which is 1.75, rounded down to 1 credit carried.
